title: Safehouse and Ghost
premise: Edmund Vasquez, a crash investigator whose family died in row twelve of Flight 4471, has spent fifteen years inside a covert analytical network that launders catastrophe data for market manipulation. When her long-dead handler sends her a meeting invitation timed to the Frankfurt open, she realizes the network that trained her is being dismantled from within—and that the crash that killed her family was its first product. To survive, Edmund must ally with the ghost's other protégés, expose the network's founder before the markets open, and choose between the loyalty that made her and the truth that unmakes her. She burns the network at dawn, but only by becoming, briefly, the thing she was trained to be.
about_author: Dominic Vane is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading accident reports before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people who know exactly how systems fail because they helped build them.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Fifteen years after the crash, Edmund works a routine investigation in Lisbon, cataloging wreckage with clinical detachment. A flashback establishes row twelve and the rules she lives by: never be seen, never ask why. Emotional beat: grief sealed under procedure. The chapter ends with an email arriving from her handler, Marcus Hale—dead eleven months.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The invitation names a time (Frankfurt open), a place (a safehouse she's never been told about), and a phrase only Marcus used. She verifies his death certificate herself. Her instinct says trap; her training says verify; her heart says go. Emotional beat: the first crack in fifteen years of control.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The Vienna safehouse is stocked with her favorite coffee, her preferred map projections—someone studied her for years. She finds Marcus's dead-drop protocol still warm. A second person arrives: Ilse Brandt, another protégé, gun first, questions second. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into wary alliance.

chapters.title: Protégés
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, with an intercut of Ilse's recollection. Three of Marcus's students converge: Edmund the investigator, Ilse the financier, Tomas Reyes the signals man. Each received the same invitation. None believes he's alive. All came anyway. Emotional beat: found family reassembling around a ghost.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. A pre-recorded briefing from Marcus plays on a timer: the network they served—Cantilever—doesn't predict disasters, it schedules them, trading on manufactured catastrophes. Flight 4471 was the proof of concept. Marcus found out and was killed for it. Emotional beat: Edmund's grief weaponized; the rules were never hers.

chapters.title: What the Training Was For
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Flashbacks to their recruitment reveal how each was chosen through loss. Ilse confesses she moved money for Cantilever knowingly for the last three years, telling herself it was hedging. Edmund refuses to absolve her. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth fractures the trio before it can hold.

chapters.title: The Frankfurt Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Marcus's cache contains a ledger of scheduled events—three entries remain live, the next timed to tomorrow's Frankfurt open. Stopping it means exposing Cantilever publicly before 9 a.m. CET, using channels they no longer control. Emotional beat: the clock becomes a character.

chapters.title: Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Cantilever counter-moves: Edmund's credentials are revoked, her name attached to a falsified incident report, arrest warrants drafted. The network that taught her invisibility now makes her visible as a criminal. Emotional beat: betrayal by the system that raised her.

chapters.title: Tomas's Frequency
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Reyes traces the invitation's true origin—not Marcus's dead hand but a live server inside Cantilever. Someone inside sent it wearing a dead man's face. Possibilities narrow to two people. Emotional beat: hope curdling into suspicion—the ghost may be hunting them.

chapters.title: The Handler's Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund decodes a second layer in Marcus's files: a personal letter admitting he recruited her because her grief made her pliable, and that he loved her like a daughter anyway. She rages, then keeps reading. Emotional beat: forgiveness contested with fury.

chapters.title: Ilse's Accounts
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse offers the one asset Cantilever can't fake: access to the trading infrastructure itself. But using it requires her to sign her name to treason. She hesitates; Edmund, remembering row twelve, tells her families aren't built on clean hands. Emotional beat: Ilse commits.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The ghost makes contact—a voice-altered call directing them to a Berlin dead drop, claiming to be Marcus's ally inside Cantilever, 'Wren.' Tomas verifies nothing; Edmund decides to trust the message, not the messenger. Emotional beat: choosing faith as a tactic, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Berlin Dead Drop
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. The drop yields Cantilever's org chart and the identity of its founder: Aldous Renner, formerly of the same regulatory body that investigated Flight 4471 and cleared it. Tomas also finds a tracker, planted en route. They've been led—or followed. Emotional beat: the plan and the trap may be the same shape.

chapters.title: Sweep
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Cantilever's cleaners hit the Vienna safehouse minutes after they evacuate. In the wreckage Edmund finds evidence Wren knew the timing exactly—which means Wren is either inside the sweep team or running it. Emotional beat: hunted, exhausted, more certain than ever.

chapters.title: Renner
chapters.summary: POV Renner, the novel's single antagonist chapter. Renner reviews the situation with calm contempt: three grieving orphans with a dead man's files. He reveals his philosophy—catastrophe is just liquidity waiting to be priced—and orders the Frankfurt event accelerated. Emotional beat: power so comfortable it doesn't need to raise its voice.

chapters.title: The Acceleration
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. The target moves up four hours; their window shrinks to pre-dawn. Ilse builds the financial kill-switch while Tomas maps broadcast paths and Edmund drafts the exposure package. Three strangers' skills click into one machine. Emotional beat: found family functioning under fire.

chapters.title: Wren Unmasked
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund baits Wren with false coordinates and catches the reply pattern: Wren is Marcus's former partner, Dana Okafor, who faked Marcus's death to protect him, then lost him anyway—and has been using his identity to finish his work. Grief recognizes grief. Emotional beat: the ghost gets a face and a wound.

chapters.title: Pre-Market
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. 3 a.m., Frankfurt. Positions set, servers warming, Renner's engineered event—a staged infrastructure failure—already in motion. Edmund must choose: stop the event quietly and save lives, or let it begin and burn Cantilever publicly with the evidence. Emotional beat: the theme made literal—loyalty vs. truth, lives vs. justice.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund finds the third option Marcus never taught her: delay the event forty minutes—enough to save the site, not enough to hide the fingerprints. It costs them surprise and nearly costs Tomas his life covering the transmission. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship; she stops following rules and starts writing them.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Open
chapters.summary: POV multiple, rapid cuts. At 9:00 CET the exposure package floods regulators, exchanges, and newsrooms simultaneously; Ilse's kill-switch freezes Cantilever's positions mid-trade; Renner is arrested boarding a private jet. The market opens on the story instead of the scheme. Emotional beat: catharsis, loud and public.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Hearings, leaks, fallout. Dana turns state's evidence; Ilse accepts a suspended sentence; Tomas disappears into a life with a garden. Edmund testifies under her real name for the first time in fifteen years. Emotional beat: visibility survived, chosen even.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund visits the rebuilt memorial wall and finds row twelve without flinching. An envelope arrives—no sender, no threat, just a meeting invitation for next spring. She smiles, pockets it, and walks out into ordinary daylight among people who know her name. Emotional beat: the invisible woman, finally at home in the light.
